description: Resilience patterns decomposed. Circuit breaker states (closed/open/half-open), bulkhead variants (thread pool, semaphore), retry strategies (exponential, decorrelated jitter), timeout (deadline, hedged request), backpressure, load shedding. The patterns that prevent cascading failure.

sub_mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker_closed_state
sub_mechanisms.definition: Normal operation. Calls pass through. Track failures within window.
sub_mechanisms.why: Default state. Reset failure count on success. Window typically 10-30s rolling.

sub_mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker_open_state
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fail fast. All calls rejected immediately without attempting. Timer until half-open.
sub_mechanisms.why: Don't waste resources on known-broken dependency. Caller sees immediate failure, can use fallback. Timeout typically 30-60s.

sub_mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker_half_open_state
sub_mechanisms.definition: Allow limited calls (often one). Success → close; failure → reopen.
sub_mechanisms.why: Probing recovery without flood. Single test request is cheap. Result determines next state.

sub_mechanisms.name: bulkhead_thread_pool
sub_mechanisms.definition: Separate thread pool per dependency. Saturation in one pool doesn't affect others.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hystrix originated. Slow dependency exhausts its pool only. Cost: thread context switching overhead.

sub_mechanisms.name: bulkhead_semaphore
sub_mechanisms.definition: Counting semaphore limits concurrent calls per dependency. Lighter than thread pool.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same isolation goal, lower overhead. No separate threads — caller blocks on permit. Used in resilience4j.

sub_mechanisms.name: exponential_backoff
sub_mechanisms.why: Don't hammer recovering dependency. Geometric growth = bounded total time. Cap at max (often 30s) to limit user wait.

sub_mechanisms.name: decorrelated_jitter
sub_mechanisms.why: Better than full jitter at preventing herd. AWS architecture blog 2015. Recommended by AWS SDK retry handlers.

sub_mechanisms.name: hedged_requests
sub_mechanisms.definition: Send request; if no response in T, send duplicate to different replica. Use first response.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reduce tail latency at cost of duplicate work. Google Tail at Scale paper. Used for read paths where duplicate cost is low.

sub_mechanisms.name: deadline_propagation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Request enters with deadline; passed through service calls; respect remaining budget.
sub_mechanisms.why: gRPC context.Deadline standard. Each service checks remaining time; abort if exceeded. Prevents wasted work after client timeout.

sub_mechanisms.name: load_shedding
sub_mechanisms.definition: Reject excess requests rather than degrade or crash. Return 503 with retry-after.
sub_mechanisms.why: Capacity-aware system. Better fast failure than slow success. Adaptive based on current load metrics.

sub_mechanisms.name: adaptive_concurrency_limit
sub_mechanisms.definition: Netflix's algorithm: gradient descent on observed latency. Concurrency limit adjusts dynamically.
sub_mechanisms.why: Manual tuning brittle. Adaptive responds to changing conditions. Netflix concurrency-limits library. Pattern in modern load balancers.

sub_mechanisms.name: fallback_response
sub_mechanisms.definition: When primary fails: return cached, default, or simplified response.
sub_mechanisms.why: Partial service > error. Cache last successful response; degraded recommendations vs no recommendations. Standard graceful degradation.

derivation_rules.name: circuit_breaker_three_state_machine_prevents_cascading
then: circuit opens → fast failure → upstream resources freed
derivation_rules.why: Without: every request waits for timeout. Threads exhausted. Cascading. With: open circuit fails in microseconds. Upstream stays healthy. Hystrix popularised, ubiquitous now.

derivation_rules.name: bulkhead_isolates_failure_domain
then: one dependency's saturation doesn't affect others
derivation_rules.why: Without: shared pool exhausted by slow dependency = all calls fail. With: only slow dependency's calls fail. Standard fault isolation.

derivation_rules.name: decorrelated_jitter_beats_full_jitter
derivation_rules.why: Full jitter still has all clients waiting on same overall distribution. Decorrelated: each next sleep depends on prev → spread broader. AWS blog measured.

derivation_rules.name: hedged_requests_reduce_tail_at_throughput_cost
then: hedged requests reduce p99 at ~2x request count
derivation_rules.why: Send to 2 replicas; use first. Slow replica's response discarded. Reduces tail (slower of two becomes fastest of two). Cost: doubled load. Used in Google's Spanner, Bigtable.

derivation_rules.name: load_shedding_better_than_uncontrolled_degradation
then: reject excess > degrade quality across all requests
derivation_rules.why: Degradation: all requests slow, eventually timeout. Shedding: some fast success + some explicit failure. Clients can retry; UX better; system stable. SRE principle.
